Applies to new volumes and snapshot copies in this region only. Existing unencrypted volumes stay unencrypted: snapshot, copy with encryption and replace them. |
| `prowler` | `ec2_networkacl_allow_ingress_any_port` | `acl-default` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, DORA RTS 2024/1774 Art.13, NIS2 CIR 2024/2690 Annex 6.7, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20, ISO27001:2022 A.8.22 |  | guidance only | No code is generated on purpose. Network ACLs are stateless and cover whole subnets, so a wrong change drops traffic at once and can lock out users. Terraform also cannot edit an entry it does not manage. Review the entries (aws ec2 describe-network-acls), then replace the open allow entry with your trusted range: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id ACL --ingress --rule-number N --protocol tcp --port-range From=443,To=443 --cidr-block TRUSTED_CIDR --rule-action allow. Keep return traffic (ephemeral ports 1024-65535) allowed. The default network ACL of a new VPC allows everything by design; security groups are the main control. |
| `prowler` | `ec2_networkacl_allow_ingress_tcp_port_22` | `acl-default` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, DORA RTS 2024/1774 Art.13, NIS2 CIR 2024/2690 Annex 6.7, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20, ISO27001:2022 A.8.22 |  | guidance only | No code is generated on purpose. Network ACLs are stateless and cover whole subnets, so a wrong change drops traffic at once and can lock out admins. Terraform also cannot edit an entry it does not manage. Replace the open entry with your admin range: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id ACL --ingress --rule-number N --protocol tcp --port-range From=22,To=22 --cidr-block ADMIN_CIDR --rule-action allow. Test access from the admin range before you remove the old entry. |
